text:
maya: Quick design q for opt-in client A/B routing — want to sketch an approach before we change SDK defaults.

maya: Problem: we need safe canaries and opt-in variants for client-side routing without forcing everyone into the new path. Also need deterministic bucketing, traceability in logs, and minimal PII leakage.

kevin: SG. Are you thinking header-based opt-in + a deterministic bucketing key?

maya: Yeah. Proposal: SDK adds an explicit opt-in header `x-rw-optin` (boolean: `1` or absent). Only SDKs that opt in will receive variant routing. We keep the default behavior unchanged.

rachel: Love opt-in. How do we ensure sticky assignment across sessions?

maya: Use `x-rw-bucket-key` if app wants sticky sessions. SDKs can default to `user_id` when available, otherwise fall back to trace id. For server-side we can also accept `x-redwood-variant` for manual overrides.

sam: Trace id as fallback is neat. Which header for trace id? We already pass `x-request-id`. Should we reuse that?

maya: Reuse `x-request-id` for correlation, but for bucketing we want a stable value per user. So SDK will compute a bucket from `user_id` or `client_generated_id`. If neither, use the first 64 bits of `trace_id` (not user-identifying).

alex: Important: we must avoid sending raw user email/PII in headers. Only opaque hashed keys. SDK should send `x-rw-bucket-key: sha256(user_id)` or similar.

kevin: Agree. Also add `x-rw-variant` (e.g. `a`, `b`, `canary-3`) in responses so clients can show feature flags for debugging. But server must sanitize to avoid feature flag leakage.

rachel: For telemetry, we should tag metrics with `rollout.variant` and `rollout.bucket_source` (user|trace|none). That makes dashboards show when sample size is sufficient.

maya: Yes. And console should show a guard: only promote variant to >20% when `min_qps` and `min_unique_users` thresholds are met. Also automatic rollback if error-rate delta > X% in the last 10m.

sam: What's reasonable X? Ops suggests 5% absolute increase in 5xx or latency p95.

alex: We should also surface cost delta per-token for each variant in rollout UX (opted into Redwood Optimize data).

kevin: Implementation sketch for SDK headers (JS):

```
// pseudo
const headers = {};
if (opts.optIn) headers['x-rw-optin'] = '1';
if (userId) headers['x-rw-bucket-key'] = sha256(userId).slice(0,16);
else headers['x-rw-bucket-key'] = traceId.slice(0,16);
// server will return x-rw-variant
```

maya: Nice. Server-side: routing policy must only consider `x-rw-bucket-key` when `x-rw-optin` present OR if caller is on allowlist (trusted internal). That prevents accidental routing from third-party clients.

rachel: Also add a per-tenant override flag in control plane (rollout target: all, only-opted, internal-only).

sam: How do we surface variant assignment in logs/traces? We tag spans with `rollout.variant` and `rollout.bucket_key_hash` (short). Avoid storing full hashed keys in long-term logs to limit retention cost.

maya: Good catch. Shorten to first 8 hex chars of hash for logs, full stored in ephemeral telemetry only for debugging.

deploy-bot: canary: started rollout canary-3 at 2% target (1768554350).

kevin: For analytics: dashboards need a new metric dimension `rollout.treatment` and the ability to filter by `opt-in` vs `global`. Also show `sample_coverage` (requests_with_bucket / total_requests).

alex: Edge case: mobile SDKs offline — they may not include `x-rw-bucket-key`. If offline, SDK should queue opt-in and re-check on next network call. Do not default to opt-in silently.

rachel: What about privacy regs? Hashing user_id is fine if salt is per-tenant and not reversible. Document salting behavior in SDK and console.

maya: Action items:
- kevin: add `x-rw-optin`, `x-rw-bucket-key` support server-side + guard rule (only-opted)
- alex: SDK change: opt-in flag + stable bucket key hashing + doc PR
- rachel: console: rollout guard thresholds, min_unique_users metric, rollback policy toggle
- sam: telemetry: add `rollout.variant`, `rollout.bucket_source`, `sample_coverage` dims

kevin: I'll open the server PR after a short spec. Will include example responses with `x-rw-variant` header and a consistent `x-request-id`.

maya: One more UX ask: in the Console rollout view show the effective sample pool size and a link to the exact query used to compute `min_unique_users` so PMs can verify.

alex: SGTM. I'll avoid changing default SDK behavior in 1.0 — opt-in only. We'll add an explicit migration plan in the SDK changelog.

rachel: If anyone is oncall tonight, heads up: canary is up at 2% starting now, watch `canary-3` tagged dashboards.

sam: I'll add a short smoke test that asserts variant header present when opt-in true.

kevin: Thanks all. I'll post a spec with header formats and example traffic-splitting math shortly.

maya: Thanks — this feels safe and reversible. :thumbsup:
